comments.text: FIXED 2026-07-16. Root cause: not a physics limit of HEM but a numerical stiffness in the rarefied emptying tail. As the pipe empties past t~0.18s a cell rarefies in a localized runaway (rho 127->23->vacuum over ~350 steps); the conservative-EEqn diagonal rho_cont*V/dt collapses to its 1e-4 floor, the solve becomes ill-conditioned, and one step tips he from 951 kJ/kg to -7.3e6 kJ/kg -> below the 273.15K (p,h) edge -> panic. Both continuity and momentum KNP dissipation independently trigger it, so it is the explicit deferred correction being over-driven in the rarefied tail, not a sign error. Fix: rarefied-tail density taper on the KNP blend beta *= clamp((rho_face-50)/(100-50),0,1), rho_face=min(rho_o,rho_nb). Dissipation zero below 50 kg/m3 (rarefied -> pure PIMPLE, stable), full above 100. Measured min dissipated-face density over the 0-0.15s ringing window is 106.5 kg/m3, so the taper is inert there. Results: full 600ms HybridAllMach completes (no panic/NaN, void in [0,1]), plateau 387.7 psia, GS-1 RMSE 30.6 psia, no cold tail; 0-0.15s ringing -55.5% and plateau retained bit-identically; default Pimple bit-identical (920 lib tests pass). title: TampinesSteamArray energy over-cooling under fast flashing (Edwards blowdown plateau under-predicted)
description:
The Edwards-O'Brien blowdown V&V test (tests/edwards_blowdown.rs) exposes an energy-conservation limitation in TampinesSteamArray::step(). During the violent subcooled->two-phase decompression the h-form energy equation loses ~10x more enthalpy than the reversible dh=dp/rho, so the bulk liquid drops to subcooled and only flashes near ambient instead of holding the ~350-380 psia (p_sat at T0~505K) flashing plateau. Measured GS-1 plateau ~17 psia vs experimental ~350-367 psia; GS-1 pressure RMSE vs digitised Data ~276 psia.

Root cause: step() runs the explicit rhoEqn continuity rho = rho_old - dt*div(phi), but correct_thermo then OVERWRITES rho with the EOS (p,h) density each inner correction. That breaks the discrete cancellation of the h*div(phi) term in d(rho h)/dt + div(phi h) = dp/dt, so enthalpy is not conserved through a fast density change. Reducing dt (30us->10us) does not fix the ratio; it is structural.

NOTE: this is the ACCURACY limitation only. The STABILITY question Ethan raised (explicit scheme cools empty pipe to ~1C and pressure rebounds past 0.42s) is CURED by our PIMPLE array: past 0.42s min T=358K, tail pressure rebound +0.9 psia, void stable 0.997 -- no artefact. See test doc comment for full V&V write-up.

Possible fixes to evaluate (need own V&V): (a) conservative (rho*e or rho*h) energy update using the continuity-consistent density rather than the EOS density in the ddt term; (b) an internal-energy (e) formulation; (c) sub-cycling the flash within the corrector. Do NOT loosen the test tolerance -- assertions there are sanity-only by design.

comments.author: teddy0@snrsiDesktop
comments.text: RESOLVED 2026-07-16. Fixed with two coupled thermodynamic corrections (no clamps): (1) conservative energy ddt using the CONTINUITY density rho_cont = rho_old - dt*div(phi) rebuilt from the final mass flux (new fvm::ddt_coeff_old), so (rho_cont-rho_old)/dt = -div(phi) exactly and the h*div(phi) term cancels term-for-term against div(phi h), restoring rho Dh/Dt = dp/dt -- this is approach (a) from the bead; (2) pressure-eqn compressibility psi = d(rho)/dp|_h (central finite-diff of the (p,h) flash at fixed enthalpy) replacing the frozen quality-weighted isothermal rho*kappa_T, which was ~100x too small in the two-phase dome and let the pressure overshoot through the plateau. Results: GS-1 flashing plateau 17 -> 393 psia (target ~350-367); RMSE vs Data 276 -> 60 psia; stable full 600 ms; no non-physical subcooling (void grows gradually, fluid holds near p_sat). All 915 lib tests still green. See collaboration/edwards_tampines_regen/debug_log.md and tests/edwards_blowdown.rs doc comment. description:
User reports (2026-07-14): after replacing fhr_sim_v2's six-group SixGroupPRKE kinetics with teh-o-prke's Nordheim-Fuchs exact timestepper (op-dt3.7 / prke_backend/mod.rs), the reactor power oscillates a lot during operation. The old PRKE-based fhr_sim_v2 did not oscillate.

Likely root cause (physics, not a code bug): Nordheim-Fuchs is a PROMPT-only excursion model -- it neglects delayed-neutron precursor dynamics entirely (documented limitation in its module doc and the user-supplied design scaffold: 'Delayed-neutron-driven operational transients should remain in the PRKE subsystem'). The old six-group PRKE carried six delayed-neutron precursor groups whose decay constants act as a low-pass filter / inertia that damps the reactivity-power-temperature feedback loop. Nordheim-Fuchs has none of that damping, so the fuel-temperature feedback loop (alpha_f*(T-T_ref) -> power -> pebble-bed heating -> T) rings.

Contributing coupling detail in the fhr_sim_v2 wiring: each 1ms step, prke_backend overwrites nordheim_fuchs.fuel_temperature with the pebble-bed TH model's temperature (the authoritative, heat-removal-aware value), then steps NF. NF also advances T internally via its own adiabatic C_f dT/dt = P. The two temperature models can disagree step-to-step, feeding the oscillation.

Candidate fixes (not yet chosen -- discuss with user):
(a) Add the 'Delayed Neutron Layer' from the outram-park-dt-plan architecture (a precursor transfer-function bank, e.g. via chem-eng transfer functions) between the prompt-excursion layer and the TH layer, restoring delayed-neutron damping.
(b) Use Nordheim-Fuchs only for prompt-critical excursion DEMOS (its intended purpose) and keep six-group PRKE for quasi-steady operation in fhr_sim_v2 -- i.e. the NF swap may be the wrong model for this always-on operational sim.
(c) Relax/filter the pebble-bed->NF fuel-temperature hand-off and/or the reactivity feedback to damp the loop numerically (a band-aid, not physical).

Regression reference: git 86ccb04 (the NF swap) + 540fd45; the pre-swap PRKE version is the parent commit of 86ccb04's prke_backend.

title: TampinesSteamArray::step() pressure oscillation with nonzero inlet velocity BC

title: Nordheim-Fuchs exact timestepper -- prompt excursion + adiabatic fuel feedback
description:
Analytical (closed-form) integrator for prompt reactivity excursions with
adiabatic fuel-temperature feedback. Scaffolded from a design doc the user
supplied 2026-07-14 (Copilot-generated, pasted in chat). Purpose is NOT
reactor safety/licensing analysis -- it is an educational/visualization
model that removes prompt-lifetime stiffness (dt << Lambda) from real-time
sims, enabling interactive HTGR/fast-reactor demos on low-power devices
(Android tablets). Positioned as the "Prompt Excursion Layer" beneath the
existing delayed-neutron PRKE precursor-bank subsystem, which stays
untouched for delayed-neutron-dominated transients.

Physical model / assumptions:
- prompt neutrons only, delayed-precursor dynamics neglected
- lumped adiabatic fuel heat capacity C_f, uniform fuel temperature T_f
- fuel-temperature feedback only: rho_f = alpha_f * (T_f - T_f_ref)
- external reactivity rho_ext held constant over a timestep
- requires alpha_f < 0 (negative feedback) for a stable closed-form
  solution -- positive-feedback excursions are intentionally out of scope

Governing equations:
  dP/dt      = P * (rho_ext + alpha_f*(T_f - T_f_ref) - beta) / Lambda
  C_f dT_f/dt = P
where P = reactor power, T_f = lumped fuel temp, C_f = fuel heat capacity,
Lambda = prompt neutron generation time, beta = delayed neutron fraction,
rho_ext = externally imposed reactivity, alpha_f = fuel feedback coeff.

Reactivity-margin substitution r = rho_ext - beta + alpha_f*(T_f - T_f_ref)
collapses this to a Riccati-type ODE:
  dr/dt = (r^2 - gamma^2) / (2*Lambda)
  gamma^2 = r_k^2 + 2*Lambda*|alpha_f|*P_k/C_f   (real-valued since alpha_f<0)

Exact per-step update (closed form, no numerical ODE integration needed):
  r_{k+1}   = -gamma * tanh( gamma*dt/(2*Lambda) + atanh(-r_k/gamma) )
  T_f,{k+1} = T_f_ref + (r_{k+1} - rho_ext + beta) / alpha_f
  P_{k+1}   = C_f/(2*Lambda*|alpha_f|) * (gamma^2 - r_{k+1}^2)

This removes the dt << Lambda stability restriction a standard ODE stepper
would need, so timestep can be chosen for UI frame rate / TH-coupling
cadence / mobile performance instead of prompt-lifetime stiffness.

Explicitly OUT of scope for this model: delayed-neutron dynamics (stays in
the existing PRKE precursor-bank subsystem), licensing/safety-grade
calculations, reactor protection analysis, spatial kinetics, fuel-melt /
severe-accident modelling. It represents only the prompt self-limiting
mechanism via adiabatic fuel heating.

Deliverable here: the timestepper itself (struct + step function) living in
teh-o-prke, uom-typed per this crate's conventions, with a doc comment
carrying the methodology above (physical quantity / valid range / units,
per the root CLAUDE.md human-interface-layer rule -- alpha_f < 0 should be
a documented precondition, not silently assumed). Add a verification test
against a known Nordheim-Fuchs benchmark case once implemented (per this
workspace's V&V documentation rule: methodology + actual measured results
in the test's doc comment). nee_soon's consumption of this as its "Prompt
Excursion Layer" interface is a separate, dependent bead.

description: Port HumidAirProp.cpp: virial coeffs (Baa/Caaa/Bww/Cwww/Baw/Caaw/Caww), enhancement factor f(T,p), psychrometric outputs (W, RH, wet-bulb, dew point, moist-air h/s/rho per kg dry air), inverse solves. Found+fixed a real bug during verification: c_aaw was missing a /rhobarstar^2=1e6 factor (CoolProp source has TWO separate /1e6 divisions for that specific correlation, unlike its sibling c_aww), which had made the third-virial correction 4 orders of magnitude too large (5.5% V error before fix, <0.1% after). Wet-bulb + dew-point IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-13 (entropy remains open).

dew_point_temperature: ported CoolProp's DewpointTemperature secant solve
almost verbatim, seeded via this crate's own vle::saturation_temperature
(IAPWS-95) in place of IF97 Tsat97. Verified: T=30C/RH=50% -> Tdp=18.451C
(matches the well-known ~18.4C psychrometric-chart value).

wet_bulb_temperature: ported CoolProp's WetBulbSolver energy-balance
residual (LHS-RHS), root-found by bisection on [T_dp, T] instead of
CoolProp's Brent-with-fallback-bracket logic -- T_wb always lies in
[T_dp, T] (standard psychrometric fact), which sidesteps needing
CoolProp's own T_sat-adjacent bracket-clamping special case entirely
(its upstream comments cite real historical bugs #2255/#2690 about that).

Caught and fixed a real bug during verification: the first implementation
evaluated liquid water's enthalpy via flash::state_pt, which only reaches
the vapour/supercritical branch (documented in its own doc comment) --
wrong branch for the subcooled liquid water present at a typical T_wb. It
silently returned a nonsense enthalpy (~-4.2e22 J/kg for liquid water at
20C/1atm) instead of erroring. Fixed by using the saturated-liquid density
at T_wb (vle::saturation_at_temperature) instead, since liquid enthalpy is
only weakly pressure-dependent -- reuses the same pattern
saturation::vbar_ws already relies on elsewhere in this module.

Verified in tests/humid_air_reference.rs: (1) exact saturation identity
T_dp=T_wb=T at R=1 (rigorous, not approximate); (2) cross-check against
Stull (2011) J.Appl.Meteor.Climatol. 50:2267-2269's independent empirical
wet-bulb formula, <0.5C (30C/50%RH: 22.00C vs Stull 22.30C; 25C/60%RH:
19.47C vs Stull 19.50C). All 6 tests in that file pass; full crate suite
(240+ tests across all files) still passes; docs/api.md regenerated.

Remaining: entropy S still needs the ideal-gas reference-state offset
calibration (separate porting effort); T_wb/T_dp still output-only, not
yet supported as input keys.
Entropy S + T_wb/T_dp as input keys IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-13.

T_wb/T_dp as inputs: psi_w_from_dew_point (exact, non-iterative -- the dew
point IS the definition) and psi_w_from_wet_bulb (bisection parameterised
by trial dew point, reusing the already-verified forward wet_bulb_temperature
as the inner black-box). Needed a targeted fix for the exact-saturation
edge case (T_wb=T at R=1): the general bisection bracket degenerates there,
and the forward solve's own secant noise (~1e-7 K) can land T_wb on either
side of T, tripping an over-tight 1e-9 K bounds check. Fixed with a direct
psi_w = psi_ws(T,p) short-circuit + loosened bounds tolerance to 1e-4 K.
Verified via round-trip (T,p,R)->T_dp/T_wb->(T,p,T_dp/T_wb)->R, <1e-4,
including the R=1 edge case.

Entropy: NOT a port of CoolProp's own ensure_ref_offsets/calc_ideal_gas_alpha0
machinery (which needs the real ideal-gas Helmholtz term + a historical
multi-point calibration) -- CoolProp's own C++ literally prints "Not
implemented" for entropy in the simplified-polynomial-enthalpy branch this
crate already uses for H, so there's no CoolProp reference implementation
to port in this configuration at all. Instead: derived via Gibbs' theorem
(pure-component ideal-gas entropies at the mixture's total T,p, Cp(T) from
the SAME polynomials already verified for H) + the standard virial/mixing
corrections, anchored to an explicit ASHRAE zero-point convention (dry air
S=0 at 0C/1atm; water's constant derived via Clausius-Clapeyron from H's
own existing 0C anchor, confirmed consistent: h_w(0C)=2501 kJ/kg matches
the known latent heat of vaporization to 3 figures, now a permanent unit
test in mod.rs).

Caught a real bug during verification: first version used dry air's own
virial-corrected molar volume (+R*ln(v_a/v_a0)) mirroring CoolProp's own
volume-based formula -- but CoolProp's version evaluates the REAL ideal-gas
Helmholtz term there (density-native), while this port integrates Cp (the
CONSTANT-PRESSURE heat capacity), so the volume form silently smuggled in
a second, spurious T-dependence (v_a is proportional to T at fixed p),
breaking dS/dT=Cp/T by ~28% at 25C. Fixed by using -R*ln(p/p0) (total
pressure, Gibbs' theorem) for both air and water instead.

Verified: dS/dT=Cp/T (rigorous, model-independent thermodynamic identity)
holds to 7e-4 to 1.2e-3 across T=1-40C, W=0-0.02 kg/kg -- small, smooth,
and of the same order as the virial correction's own size (consistent with
a residual virial-cross-term path-dependence artifact, not a remaining bug).
CAVEAT, documented in the module doc: S's absolute value is NOT verified
against CoolProp or an external table (different reference-state convention
than CoolProp's own, and H's own mixture value already has a known ~6.6
kJ/kg ASHRAE offset that S likely inherits) -- only the temperature
dependence is rigorously verified. Full crate suite (241+ lib tests, 10 in
humid_air_reference.rs) passes; docs/api.md regenerated.

Remaining open in this bead: absolute-value cross-check for S against a
real external reference, if/when op-kbc.3 (rfluids oracle) lands.

title: TransferFnFirstOrder response_vec growth in real-time loops (DelayedNeutronLayer / NF reactivity driver)
description: TransferFnFirstOrder (chem-eng) accumulates one FirstOrderResponse per input change and only clears after 20*tau. In DelayedNeutronLayer the slowest group (tau~80s) means the vector can grow to ~1.6M entries (20*80s at 1ms) before clearing in the always-on fhr_sim_v2 GUI loop, with O(n) per-step summation -> memory + slowdown over long real-time runs. Not a correctness issue (superposition is exact) and fine for the bounded headless regression tests (~seconds). Options: (a) add an exponential-integrator fast path to TransferFnFirstOrder / FirstOrderStableTransferFnNoZeroes that keeps O(1) state, or (b) periodic rebase of the lag to its current offset. Same concern applies to nordheim_fuchs's reactivity driver when the input changes every step. Surfaced during op-dt3.11.
close_reason: Reimplemented DelayedNeutronLayer with direct implicit (backward-Euler) precursor time-stepping, replacing the 5 TransferFnFirstOrder lags whose response_vec grew unboundedly (O(n)/step). Per-group update C_i^{n+1}=(C_i^n+dt*(beta_i/Lambda)*P)/(1+dt*lambda_i), same discretisation as SixGroupPRKE's coefficient matrix but decoupled from the prompt equation (Nordheim-Fuchs owns prompt). Holds only 5 f64 precursor states -> O(1) time+memory, no growing Vec, no TransferFnFirstOrder. Public API unchanged (new/u235_five_group/advance/total_delayed_neutron_fraction/decay_constants/delayed_fractions/last_delayed_increment), so no consumer edits needed (fhr_sim_v2 in engine+tampines, htgr_sim_v1). VERIFIED: physics identical to old fix -- oscillation regression prompt-only 194.23 MW p2p -> delayed-layer 0.0086 MW (both fhr_sim_v2 copies); teh-o-prke 21 lib tests pass. PERF: new O(1) perf test (100k-step early vs late blocks after 20x more steps) -- late/early ratio 0.31, ~4-14 ns/step flat, vs old ~49us->1.8ms/step linear growth. Builds clean: teh-o-prke, engine fhr_sim_v2+htgr_sim_v1, tampines fhr_sim_v2. See op-dt3.11. Note under op-e46.

description: Follow-ups surfaced by genfoam thermoMechanics mesh solve (op-p6p.11). title: Velocity/Reynolds-dependent pipe-38 form loss to fix coupled DRACS low-flow cases (B1/C1)
description:
Follow-up to op-4wl.2/op-4wl.4 (pipe-38 K=0.8->17.8 SAM adoption, 2026-07-15). A single uniform form loss K=17.8 fixes the mid/high-flow DRACS over-prediction but cannot fix the two lowest-flow coupled cases B1 (655W) and C1 (841W), which already under-predict at K=0.8 and worsen to -6.62%/-6.80% under added resistance (form loss ~ v^2, negligible at low flow). They currently carry a documented per-point widened DRACS tolerance (B1 0.062->0.0676; C1 0.0676->0.069).

Proper fix: give pipe 38 a velocity/Reynolds-dependent loss of the form f_darcy = form_loss + b*Re^c, which is ALREADY supported by InsulatedFluidComponent::new_custom_component (see insulated_pipes_and_fluid_components/mod.rs:204, new_custom_component with reynolds_coefficient b and reynolds_power c). Shape needed: small a at low Re (helps B1/C1 low-flow under-prediction) rising to ~K=17.8-equivalent at high Re (preserves the mid/high-flow over-prediction fix). Calibrate b,c across all 25 coupled cases; re-validate the isolated-DRACS SAM reference (currently defined at constant K=17.8); then tighten B1/C1 tolerances back to the benchmark bound (0.062/0.0676) and recompute regression literals. Deferred from op-4wl.4 because per-iteration cost is a full ~50-min 25-case run and it would also require re-deriving the isolated SAM calibration.

TampinesSteamArray::correct_thermo() (crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/openfoam_algorithms/rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs, from op-21g.10) calls t_ph_eqm/v_ph_eqm/kappa_t_ph_eqm/mu_ph_eqm/lambda_ph_eqm/cp_ph_eqm directly per cell -- these PANIC (not Result) if (p,h) falls out of the valid IAPWS-IF97 range (e.g. below 273.15K), unlike OPCPFluidArray::correct_thermo() (outram-park-fork-coolprop), which does 'if let Ok(state) = flash::state_ph(...) { update } else { keep previous rho/T/psi for this cell }' -- a graceful degradation, not a panic, if a cell wanders out of range mid-simulation.

Fix direction (not yet decided/implemented): either (a) wrap the tampines-steam-tables (p,h) flash calls in a fallible variant if one exists or can be added, matching CoolProp's graceful-degradation pattern, or (b) some other guard against out-of-range panics during a running PIMPLE loop.

User explicitly deferred this (2026-07-13) -- wants to check the situation manually first before any fix is attempted. Do not implement without further discussion.
close_reason: Decided against: user (2026-07-14) wants panic-on-out-of-range, not graceful degradation like OPCPFluidArray -- a stale-state fallback would silently produce a nonphysical cell state during a running PIMPLE loop, which is worse than a loud crash. Verified there is nothing to change: t_ph_eqm/v_ph_eqm/kappa_t_ph_eqm/mu_ph_eqm/lambda_ph_eqm/cp_ph_eqm already return plain uom values (no Result to unwrap) and already panic!() deep in ph_flash_region -> check_if_within_ph_validity_region on out-of-range (p,h). correct_thermo() as committed in 356daff already has the desired behavior.

title: Pipe transient (dynamic) Brent-based cell-network solver
description: DWSIM Pipe.vb's RunDynamicModel: represents a pipe as a chain of accumulation-stream cells, solves inter-cell mass flow via Brent root-find on the pressure-difference residual per timestep (compressible, volume-conserving). Deferred -- op-qo2.1 only ports the steady-state correlations (Beggs-Brill/Lockhart-Martinelli/Darcy-Weisbach); tampines' own single_phase (TUAS FluidArray) / compressible (OPCPFluidArray) wrappers already provide transient pipe behavior for their respective backends.
close_reason: Ported from DWSIM Pipe.vb's RunDynamicModel(): src/pipe/transient.rs -- PipeCell (fixed-volume mass-balance accumulator, density = mass/volume, advance_mass_balance() over a timestep) and solve_intercell_mass_flow() (Brent root-find on the pressure-drop residual, DWSIM's Pdrop_transition - dpt(mass_flow) = 0). Used the roots crate's existing Brent implementation (BSD-2-Clause, already an approved workspace dependency, not yet used elsewhere) rather than hand-rolling one, since Brent's method itself is standard numerical-methods machinery, not DWSIM-specific -- added roots.workspace = true to this crate's Cargo.toml. DWSIM's IPOPT least-squares fallback (when Brent fails to converge) was not replicated -- Brent's own SearchError is surfaced directly instead, and this crate has no IPOPT-equivalent solver to reach for regardless. The (V,T)->P flash DWSIM does per cell after each mass transfer is explicitly left to the caller (same flash-dependency pattern as heat_exchanger/expander/pump). 4 new tests (46 total, 0 warnings): forward-flow and reverse-flow root-finding against a linear resistance model, and PipeCell mass-balance/density sanity checks. cargo build/test --release and cargo doc (deny broken-intra-doc-links) both pass clean.
